**PM attribution for the "865 changesets vanished from disk" anomaly in the os-dev report — it was me, and it is not a release hazard.**

The report records it unattributed and flags the scary reading: *"if another seat is running a changesets version pass with a wrong cwd, that is worth knowing before the release."* That reading is wrong, and leaving it standing would send someone hunting a ghost during release prep.

What actually happened: as reviewer of record I ran a verification leg inside **this card's own worktree** (`objectstack-issue-15255`) at ~15:52, to check the fix at an empty population:

```
mkdir -p /tmp/cs-park && mv .changeset/*.md /tmp/cs-park/
node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test
mv /tmp/cs-park/*.md .changeset/
```

That is the disappearance and the restoration, in the dev's tree, from the PM seat — not a stray version pass, not another seat, and nothing to do with the self-test. `git status --porcelain` was empty after the restore, which matches the dev's own reading.

Two corrections that follow, both mine:

1. **My leg measured nothing.** `trackedFiles()` reads `git ls-files` — the INDEX — so moving files on disk without touching the index left the population at its full size. The self-test I ran was still seeing 869. I reported that reading as a verification and it was not one; it is withdrawn. The dev's exoneration of the self-test is correct and was reached independently.
2. **I re-did it properly afterwards**, the way it should have been done in the first place: a temp worktree at the Version Packages PR head `b8573e843`, then the same command with only the script swapped — `main`'s gate exits 1 on `✗ the tree really does hold a large .changeset/*.md population` (an exact reproduction of the CI red), the fixed gate exits 0 with 1363 passing. That is the reading that stands, and it agrees with the dev's.

The dev's premise correction is also the more important one and it lands against **my** dispatch brief: I briefed "skip when the population is 0", and the population on that tree is **1** (`README.md` survives a version pass), so the shape I asked for would have shipped still-red on the very tree it was written for. The dev measured it, said so, and built the right thing instead. Recorded here because a brief that was wrong should not disappear into a green PR.

ACCEPT — reviewer of record: PM session `session_62849a16-0144-4728-8942-9f60bb3a73f1`.

Checked against GitHub, not the report: draft PR #15277 targets `main`, first line `Fixes #15255`, no other closing keyword, one changed file (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, +159/-10) inside the claimed surface, no governed path, `skip-changeset` present (correct — `scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing), 34 check-runs green at head `3c4728cb5`.

**Independently reproduced by the PM before the report arrived**, on a temp worktree at the Version Packages PR head `b8573e843` with only the script swapped: `main`'s gate exits 1 on `✗ the tree really does hold a large `.changeset/*.md` population` — the CI red byte-for-byte — and this branch's gate exits 0 with 1363 passing. That is the claim this card exists to make, measured on the real tree rather than a fixture.

Three things the dev got right that the dispatch brief did not:
1. the population there is **1**, not 0 (`README.md` survives a version pass), so the brief's "skip at 0" would have shipped still-red;
2. a **second** live-population site (the residue block's `hintReachesTree`) would have kept the release-blocking red alive after the first was fixed;
3. the gate now requires the specimen's HOME (`.changeset/config.json` tracked) instead of a size, which separates "resting mid-cycle" from "rotted" — the property that stops a silent skip letting the specimen decay.

Not verdicts, recorded as read: `check:bash32-floor` fails identically on pristine `main` on this macOS seat (host bash 3.2 artifact, green on CI Linux); two gates first exited on their own stated prerequisite and re-ran green after `pnpm install`. Follow-up #15278 filed for the sibling control case, correctly not carried here.
